correctness.rationale: Reconstructed from actual frozen RESULT.md: bisector unit normals yield M(omega)=I−2omega diag(p,q)+omega²(p,q)(p,q)^T for expected coordinate squares, with p=(1+c)/2,q=(1−c)/2. Its positive offdiagonal for omega>0 makes Perron root the exact asymptotic expected squared norm factor for any nonzero deterministic starting error. Conditional energy identity and positive definite average Gram yield convergence iff 0<omega<2. For stable omega, rank-one secular equation 1=omega S(z) with z=delta/omega in (0,2q); S strictly increases from 1/2 to infinity, parametrizing omega∈(0,2), and derivative S−zS′=2F has strictly negative derivative −zS″ for z>0, so unique optimizer. At c=0 symmetry yields omega*=1. At c>0 the derivative of rho at omega=1 equals −2pq c²/(p²+q²)<0, giving strict overrelaxation. Near parallel q↓0, critical balance 2q−z~2q^(3/2) implies optimized spectral gap~4q versus default 2q. All boundary quantifiers and the excluded singular c=1 were checked. Independent new SymPy/algebraic replay 7 identities plus eight high-precision representative values; tests are corroboration only, not infinite proof.

evidence: Rank-one secular optimum and nonzero derivative at omega=1 constitute substantial exact optimization
Near parallel comparison delta*(q)~4q versus delta_standard(q)~2q yields exact asymptotic factor 2
The comparable cyclic two-row relaxation optimum is distinct, underscoring need to distinguish algorithm and metric.
value.rationale: Constant-relaxation choice in two-row uniformly randomized Kaczmarz is a natural measurable performance question whose exact annealed asymptotic factor differs from one-step energy bounds and deterministic cyclic sweeps. The unique root characterization spans every nonorthogonal angle, reveals overrelaxation is strictly optimal for all nonorthogonal rows, and gives a sharp limiting factor-two improvement in spectral gap for nearly parallel lines. It is a nontrivial precise benchmark for stochastic projection dynamics rather than a relabeled standard upper bound or a tiny isolated numerical gain; no claim for finite horizon, general sampling, almost-sure exponents or more rows.
residual_risks: Practical value for many-row/noisy Kaczmarz not established; contribution is a sharp natural small model.
